requirement:
# REQ-2234: The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2234

#### Bug description

The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true. This has happened since version 3.1.1. It still worked in 3.1.0.

story.summary: The agent changed the shared member-collection code in TypeCollector so it no longer crashes on invalid key layouts. For mixed int/string keys, it now reports the diagnostic and skips the member (`continue`). For duplicate int or string keys, it guards each `Dictionary.Add` with `ContainsKey`. It adds analyzer tests for `[MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)]` types, execution tests showing such a type gets no generated formatter and still round-trips at run time, and a README section describing which diagnostics apply to suppressed types.
story.why: Issue #2234 says the analyzer stopped reporting diagnostics for SuppressSourceGeneration types in 3.1.1. The visible fix implies the root cause was an exception thrown while collecting members with duplicate or mixed keys, which kills the analyzer. However, nothing in the diff touches SuppressSourceGeneration-specific logic. The reviewer cannot confirm from the diff alone that this is the 3.1.0 → 3.1.1 regression rather than a separate crash.
touches_beyond_requirement: The TypeCollector changes apply to every [MessagePackObject] type, including ones that do get a generated formatter, not only suppressed types.
A new README section documents analyzer behavior for suppressed types, including which rules are and are not reported.
Execution tests check run-time round-tripping and that no generated formatter exists; this is beyond the analyzer bug.
story.confidence_overview: Medium that the crash-avoidance edits are correct for the duplicate and mixed-key cases; the new tests cover these. Low-to-medium that this is the whole fix for the reported regression: the diff shows no change to any SuppressSourceGeneration branch. It is unclear whether tests such as MemberWithoutKeyIsReported would have failed before the change. High that the new tests exist and assert specific diagnostics.

claims.text: The README documents that suppressed types are still validated for MsgPack004, MsgPack005, MsgPack015, MsgPack003 and MsgPack012, but not for MsgPack011, MsgPack016 or MsgPack017.

When a member's key kind (int vs string) differs from the other members, TypeCollector reports DoNotMixStringAndIntKeys and skips that member instead of continuing with a null key. This applies in both member-collection paths (properties and fields).
claims.requirement_quote: The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true.

claims.text: A duplicate int or string key no longer causes Dictionary.Add to throw. The second member with the same key is not added; the existing duplicate-key diagnostic is expected to have been reported earlier.
claims.requirement_quote: The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true.

claims.text: Scope: the TypeCollector edits are not limited to suppressed types. They change collection for every MessagePackObject type, including generated ones. No public API, rule descriptor or wire-format code is changed.

The analyzer tests assert that suppressed types still get MsgPack004 (missing Key), MsgPack015 (AllowPrivate required), MsgPack003 (member type not serializable) and MsgPack005 (duplicate or mixed keys) at specific locations. This is the test evidence for the requirement. The diff does not show whether the first three cases failed before this change.
claims.requirement_quote: The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true.

claims.text: For a suppressed type, the test expects no diagnostics at all when it has a private keyed field with AllowPrivate, an init-only property and a non-partial class. In other words, it expects MsgPack011, MsgPack016 and MsgPack017 not to be reported.
A suppressed type gets no formatter from GeneratedMessagePackResolver and still serializes and deserializes through the standard dynamic resolver.

refusals.what: README section declaring which analyzer rules do and do not apply to SuppressSourceGeneration types (MsgPack011/016/017 excluded).
refusals.why: This is user-facing documentation of analyzer policy, added beyond the bug fix. A maintainer should confirm this is the intended contract.

refusals.what: Source generator behavior on duplicate keys changes from an exception to silently keeping only the first member.
refusals.why: This may change generated formatter output for invalid inputs rather than failing. A maintainer should confirm a diagnostic always blocks the build in this case.

findings.description: Duplicate-keyed members are now silently dropped instead of throwing. reportDiagnostic is invoked with ?. so it may be null in some paths. If this code runs in the source generator with no diagnostic sink, a formatter could be generated that omits a member, where the build previously failed loudly. Verify that a diagnostic is always surfaced when this branch is taken.

No hunk touches SuppressSourceGeneration handling. The fix only prevents crashes on duplicate or mixed keys, which affect all types. If the 3.1.1 regression was an early return or skip for suppressed types, it may not be fixed. Confirm that MemberWithoutKeyIsReported, AllowPrivateRequiredIsReported and MemberTypeMustBeMessagePackObjectIsReported failed before this change, or that the original repro case was duplicate keys.
The README states MsgPack012 (type accessibility) is still reported for suppressed types, but no new test covers MsgPack012 for a suppressed type.

The new 'continue' skips the rest of the loop body for the mismatched member. That means later per-member processing (formatter attribute lookup, hiddenIntKey increment) no longer runs for it. This only matters on the error path, but it changes what other diagnostics may be reported for that member.
